text:
Incident Bot: PAGER: gen-runtime-eu-primary kernel-panic spike — 40% of pods restarted in last 12m, increased 502s and streaming truncation, alert: INC-REDWOOD-9876

Alex Kim: taking primary (oncall) — will triage, handing to me if I need to bounce nodes :handshake:

Maria Chen: I'm covering secondary/clinical fallback — can take traffic shift if you need, also can follow rollback plan

Jamal Ortiz: quick observability summary — p95->p99 jumped, p99 gen latency eu-west-1 = 3.5s (baseline 0.9s), 502 ratio up to 2.3% last 10m. KV cache hit rate steady. CPU spikes on prim-GPU-nodes, dmesg shows repeated NVRM kernel errors on 3 nodes. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc/gen-runtime-eu?from=now-30m&to=now

Alex Kim: ok that's kernel-level. Initial mitigation plan: 1) shift new traffic off prim pool to sec pool 2) drain and reboot affected prim nodes 3) enable read-only fallback for long-running streams 4) monitor customer impact + rollback path

Maria Chen: will stand by to receive traffic. command to scale routing (control plane):
```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/api/v1/routing/weights \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN' \
 -d '{"route":"gen-eu","weights":{"prim-eu":0.0,"sec-eu":1.0}}'
```
I'll run that in 2m unless Alex says otherwise.

Alex Kim: do it. point to note: keep 5% at prim for canary for 10m then 0.

Maria Chen: applied weight change -> prim-eu 5% -> sec-eu 95% (will drop to 0% in 10m) :white_check_mark:

SRE Runbook Bot: Runbook: gen-runtime-kernel-panic -> https://runbooks.redwood.example/kernel-panic-gen-runtime
Steps: verify kernel logs, annotate nodes, drain, reboot, reprovision driver, monitor NVML errors.

Jamal Ortiz: logs (tail) from node prim-gpu-03:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65): 79, PID: 3421
[ 1234.570000] kernel: watchdog: tasks blocked for more than 120 seconds.
```
Looks like NV driver panic.

Liz Park: support side: we've flagged top 8 customers with open streams in eu-west and notified them with a short advisory. CS contacts: @cs-eu on the thread. So far two customers reported truncated responses in streaming; both on hosted tier, not dedicated.

Alex Kim: short checklist for handoff (to whoever picks up):
- Current status: traffic shifted -> prim 5% -> sec 95% (10m canary), will go to 0% at +10m unless errors
- Affected nodes: prim-gpu-01, prim-gpu-03, prim-gpu-07 (kernel oops)
- Mitigations in progress: routing shift, node drains queued, reboot scheduled for prim-gpu-03 now
- Customer impact: streaming truncation + increased p99; ~0.5% active sessions affected, two reported tickets
- Escalation contacts: infra-hardware@redwood, driver-eng oncall (pager), cloud-provider support link in #vendors

Maria Chen: I set an automation to auto-scale sec pool by +2 replicas to absorb burst: autoscaler triggered -> sec pool +2 (now 12 replicas)

Jamal Ortiz: monitoring hooks added:
- Alert adjusted: INC-REDWOOD-9876 -> suppress new duplicate pages for 15m
- Synthetic stream job frequency increased to every 30s for eu-west

Alex Kim: reboot complete on prim-gpu-03, driver reinstall in progress (ansible). If reinstall doesn't clear NV errors we will mark node as quarantine and reprovision.

SRE Runbook Bot: driver reinstall command:
```
ansible-playbook -i inventory/prim-gpu-hosts reboot-and-install-nvidia.yml -e "node=prim-gpu-03"
```
Note: confirm kernel-headers match driver version before restart.

Maria Chen: after 10m canary timer hit -> I moved prim-eu to 0% traffic. sec-eu now handling full load. :ok_hand:

Alex Kim: good. leaving a note: do not reintroduce prim nodes until NV errors dropped and synthetic jobs show stable p99 for 20m.

Liz Park: opened support incident SR-7789 for the two affected customers, templated message posted, will update if they escalate.

Jamal Ortiz: long-term follow-ups to track in the incident doc: kernel/driver regression, host firmware checks, soak test after reprovision, and possible move to newer driver 525.x in staging.

Alex Kim: handing off primary to Maria for next shift. My phone is available if needed: +1-555-01-ALEX.

Maria Chen: taking primary. Handoff notes for next oncall (copy/paste):
- Current state: sec-eu primary routing, prim pool quarantined (3 nodes)
- Must monitor: p99 gen latency, 502 rate, synthetic streams green for 20m before reintroducing nodes
- Quick commands: routing weights curl above, ansible reboot above, grafana & logs links
- Postmortem owner: Alex (initial), Maria (follow through on hardware ticket)

Maria Chen: I'm going to follow driver reinstall results and the infra ticket. If NV errors persist after reprovisioning -> escalate to vendor support and prepare to reprovision affected hosts from scratch.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-REDWOOD-9876 status update -> mitigated to "degraded"; primary pool quarantined; customer impact limited, support tickets created.

Alex Kim: thanks team. leaving now. Maria, take it from here.

Maria Chen: acknowledged. I'll post updates in this thread and in #incidents when we move to resolved.

Liz Park: tagging CS team and product for awareness: @product, @cs-eu. I'll push updates to customer-facing channel if anything changes.

SRE Runbook Bot: Suggested post-incident actions: schedule kernel-driver compatibility test on staging, add NVML OOM alert threshold, add a playbook snippet for rapid routing swaps.

Maria Chen: logging final note for this handoff: next update planned in 20m or on major state change.

Alex Kim: :wave:
